crossings.description: Pedestrian crossings over one or more movements.

demand.description:
Portal demand generators; when non-empty they replace the static
walking-skeleton population.

id.description: Stable scenario identifier recorded in run provenance.

movements.description: Movement connectors from one portal to another along a guide path.

population.description: Walking-skeleton population tuning, used only when `demand` is empty.

portals.description: Entry and exit points attached to path ends.

profiles.description: Passenger-car physical and behavior profile distributions.

regions.description: Closed polygons marking traversable areas other than guide paths.

rules.description: Right-of-way or control rules attached to movements.

schema_version.description: Schema version the document was written against.

signals.description: Fixed-time signal controllers with phased signal heads.

ConflictRegionSource.description:
An authored conflict region shared by two movements.

The geometry lets a renderer or metric show where two movement envelopes
cross; the movement pair is what a signal check uses to reject conflicting
greens. A scenario may author it explicitly or, later, accept a derived one.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

movements.description: Exactly two movements whose envelopes conflict in this region.

CoordinateSystem.description: Human-facing names for the world coordinate axes.

x.description: Name of the positive x axis, for example `east_m`.

y.description: Name of the positive y axis, for example `north_m`.

CrossingSource.description: A pedestrian crossing occupying a traversable region over some movements.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

DemandSource.description:
One portal demand generator: arrivals at an entry portal and the routes
those vehicles take.

A demand source names an entry portal (the `from` portal of one or more
movements) and a mean arrival rate. Each generated vehicle is assigned one
of the listed movements by relative weight, so route assignment is scenario
data rather than a simulator branch.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

portal.description: Entry portal where generated vehicles enter the world.

rate_vph.description: Mean arrival rate in vehicles per hour.

routes.description: Movements a generated vehicle may follow, with relative weights.

MovementSource.description:
A movement connector from one portal to another along a guide path.

A movement is the Phase 1 routing primitive: it names where an agent enters
the modeled area, where it leaves, and the guide path between them. Conflict
regions, crossings, and control rules all reference movements rather than
naming a scenario kind, so a layout such as a four-leg intersection is data,
not a simulator branch.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

priority.description: Right-of-way rank; a lower value is honored before a higher one.

PathEnd.description: Which end of a path a portal is attached to.

oneOf.description: The first vertex of the path.
The last vertex of the path.

PathSource.description: One authored guide path as an ordered polyline.

id.description: Stable path identifier, unique across all authored objects.

points.description: Ordered vertices of the guide path.

PolygonSource.description:
A closed polygon in metres.

The ring closes implicitly from the last vertex back to the first, so the
authored vertex list must not repeat the first point at the end.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

vehicle_count.description: Number of vehicles introduced on the guide path.

vehicle_spacing_m.description: Longitudinal gap between adjacent vehicles in metres.

vehicle_speed_mps.description: Constant vehicle speed in metres per second.

PortalSource.description: An entry or exit point attached to one end of a path.

end.description: Which end of the path the portal marks.

id.description: Stable portal identifier, unique across all authored objects.

path.description: Identifier of the path this portal belongs to.

width_m.description: Traversable width of the portal in metres.

ProfileRangeSource.description:
An inclusive uniform distribution for one profile parameter.

A range with `min == max` is a constant. The owning field name carries the
physical unit, for example `speed_mps` or `time_gap_s`.

ProfileSource.description:
Passenger-car physical and behavior profile distributions.

Every generated vehicle samples one value from each range from the `profile`
random stream, so its body and longitudinal behavior are stable for the run.
Pedestrian profiles are Increment 3 work.

comfortable_brake_mps2.description: Comfortable deceleration in metres per second squared.

max_accel_mps2.description: Maximum acceleration in metres per second squared.

speed_mps.description: Desired free-flow speed in metres per second.

time_gap_s.description: Desired following time gap in seconds.

RouteShareSource.description: One movement's relative share of a demand source's arrivals.

weight.description: Relative weight; a larger weight is chosen proportionally more often.

RuleKind.description: How a movement's right of way is controlled.

oneOf.description: No control; the movement proceeds subject to ordinary interaction.
The movement must yield to the conflicting movements.
The movement must stop before proceeding.
A signal controller governs the movement.

RuleSource.description: A control rule attached to one movement.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

kind.description: Kind of control the rule applies.

signal.description: Signal controller, present exactly when `kind` is `signal`.

SignalColor.description: Display color of one signal head during one phase.

oneOf.description: The controlled movement should prepare to stop.

SignalHeadSource.description: One signal head controlling a movement.

id.description: Identifier unique within the owning signal.

states.description: The color of every head in the owning signal during this phase.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across all authored objects.

phases.description: Phases in cycle order, each showing every head once.

SignalStateSource.description: One head's color during one phase.

color.description: Color shown on that head during this phase.

head.description: Head identifier within the owning signal.
